chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Maysara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The ablution is one (washing), one (washing), and he described the ankle as being on the back of the foot.
ai.seo_question: How many times should each part be washed during wudu according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the fundamental rule of washing limbs once during wudu, a key point of distinction in Shia jurisprudence against the Sunni view of washing three times. It provides precise anatomical guidance by defining the 'ankle' (ka'b) as located on the dorsal aspect of the foot, ensuring the correct boundaries for washing the feet are met. This narration is part of the extensive chain of transmission (isnad) in Al-Kafi, highlighting the reliability of the Ahl al-Bayt's practical teachings on ritual purity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Abu Dawood, altogether from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Ali Bin Al Mugheira, from Maysara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Ablution (Wudhu) is one (washing), one (washing)’, and heasws described the ankles regarding the back of the feet’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and abu Dawud all from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from Ali ibn al-Mughirah from Maysarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Wudu’ is one (washing of the face and hands) and one (wiping of the head and feet).’ He (the Imam) then explained about the ankle in the back of the foot.’”
